o1.biggest_strength: It correctly rejects the ₹1.86 crore draft, puts cash into the top 5 matte shades, starts re-cartoning on Monday, and avoids ordering liquid lipstick or glitter palettes.
o1.biggest_mistake: It assumes the held top-5 units are inside the 9,100 on hand, so it invents a 1–8 December stock gap and recommends pausing demand when the re-carton plus rush order should mostly bridge the sale risk.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Rework the top-5 stock math to show 13,000 units after re-cartoning, remove unnecessary demand suppression, and tighten the rush/standard quantities around that corrected cover.

o2.biggest_strength: It gives a clear cash-safe PO plan, sizes the rush order against the sale-week spike, keeps slow lines out of the buy, and adds a useful pro pre-book move for bridal artists.
o2.biggest_mistake: It also gets the re-cartoning math wrong by saying the top 5 still have only 2.4 weeks after re-cartoning, instead of lifting to about 13,000 units and 3.4 weeks of cover.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Correct the re-cartoned top-5 stock position, place the standard POs on Monday rather than waiting until Friday, and adjust the December back-order plan so it only triggers if sell-through beats plan.

reason: I would rather use Output 2 because its order sizing and operating rules are a little sharper and less likely to suppress demand. Both are strong, but both miss the same important held-stock signal, so neither is clean as-is.
